newsitem.title: UK: Supermarkets face tough 9 mths - ASDA head.
newsitem.headline: Supermarkets face tough 9 mths - ASDA head.

text.p: British supermarkets are likely to see tough trading conditions for the next six to nine months, ASDA chief executive Allan Leighton told Reuters.
"I think the markets are tough...it is going to be like that for the next six to nine months," he said in an interview.
Leighton, who has just taken over from Archie Norman as he becomes chairman, said the food retail market was "pretty static."
He said there were "some economic factors...working for us, there is a bit more inflation."
But overall the market was very competitive, he added.
"Everybody's margin is going down...that's generally a sign of it being very competitive," he said.
In addition, a petrol price war between oil majors and the supermarkets, which has only recently showed signs of abating, has had an impact, he said.
"You have (also) had the petrol issue as well which has affected us all," he said.
